one-line thesis: SEDEMAC delivered a breakout FY26 with 61% revenue growth to INR 1,058 Cr, driven by regulatory-mandated ISG adoption in 2/3-wheelers and robust industrial genset demand. The investment case hinges on the proprietary sensorless control technology enabling cost-effective integration (ISG+EFI) and expansion into high-volume power tools and commercial vehicles, funding organic capex with >40% RoCE.
financial scorecard: Revenue: INR 1,058 Cr (+61% YoY); EBITDA: >INR 200 Cr (~21% margin, up due to operating leverage); PAT: >INR 100 Cr (normalized, no major one-offs cited); Order Book: Not explicitly quantified but implied strong via 3.9M units sold (+60% YoY); Net Debt: Low leverage implied by funding growth via internal accruals and modest working capital intensity.
guidance: Revenue Growth: Continued double-digit growth expected from new motorcycle launches (3 top-10 models) and EV MCU ramp; Margin: Mild pressure expected from commodity inflation and semiconductor tightness; Order Inflow: Strong visibility from ISG+EFI integration and export 3W ramp; Capex: MF3 (ECU) commissioning Q2FY27, MF4 (Electric Machines) Q3FY27.
order book & pipeline: Proxy via unit sales: 3.9 million control-intensive ECUs in FY26 (+60% YoY); 80% of incremental ISG volume in India captured by SEDEMAC; SOP achieved for export 3W ISG in Q4FY26.
segment / subsidiary detail: Mobility: Dominant in ICE 2/3W ISG (OBD-II driver), ramping EV MCUs (e2W/e3W); Industrial: Genset controllers (North America market share gain via default adoption by leader); New: Power tools (first biz win, SOP in 4-5 quarters), Commercial Vehicle after-treatment (SOP H2FY27).
growth verticals / optionality: Power tools market (300M units/year potential); Sensorless EV MCU global differentiation; ISG+EFI integrated unit adoption reducing OEM BOM; Export penetration beyond Indian OEM exports to direct global Japanese/Chinese OEMs.
margins & cost dynamics: FY26 EBITDA margin ~21%; Near-term headwinds from commodity inflation and semiconductor supply tightness expected to cause mild margin pressure; Long-term margins protected by proprietary sensorless tech and high switching costs.
capex / expansion: Cumulative plant capex INR 227 Cr (as of Mar-25); MF3 (120k sq ft, 3x ECU capacity) shipments Q2FY27; MF4 (Electric Machines) shipments Q3FY27; Land acquired in Shoolagiri for southern India presence; Capex intensity ~20-22% of incremental revenue.
capital allocation: Growth funded primarily by internal accruals (EBIT ~15%); Working capital intensity ~13-15% of revenue; No dividend discussion; Focus on reinvestment for capacity and R&D (cumulative INR 256 Cr).
risks & watch-items: Customer concentration (top 1 minus next 4 metric improving but still relevant); Commodity/semiconductor cost inflation; El Nino impact on monsoon (domestic 2W demand) and US hurricanes (genset demand); R&D execution risk in new segments (CV, Power Tools).
management quality / tone: Confident and data-driven; Emphasized technology moat (sensorless) and regulatory tailwinds; Transparent on risks (surveyed investors); Conservative on specific forward-looking product revenue splits but aggressive on volume trends.
non-obvious takeaways: Sensorless technology eliminates physical sensors entirely (not just reduces count), solving reliability issues (water/dust ingress) in EVs and enabling ISG in wet-magneto engines where competitors fail; ISG+EFI integration creates a 'hard to argue against' economic proposition for OEMs despite potential single-source hesitation.
challenges → beneficiaries & losers:
| Challenge | Beneficiary/Loser | Dir | Conviction | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Regulatory push for OBD-II and emission norms drives mandatory ISG adoption; SEDEMAC holds ~80% share of incremental ISG volume. | Bajaj Auto | beneficiary | High | Top 3 OEM using SEDEMAC ISG; launching 3 new top-10 models with SEDEMAC ISG in FY27. |
| Need for reliable, cost-effective EV motor controllers without sensor failure risks. | TVS Motor Company | beneficiary | High | Adopter of ISG in Jupiter/XL100; likely partner for sensorless EV MCU given SEDEMAC's tech lead. |
| US Genset manufacturers facing need for efficient, compliant engine controls. | Cummins India | beneficiary | Med | SEDEMAC gained default adoption with a North American genset leader; potential indirect beneficiary if domestic manufacturing aligns. |
| Legacy sensor-based MCU suppliers facing obsolescence in harsh environments. | Unorganized EV Component Suppliers | loser | High | SEDEMAC's sensorless tech eliminates failure points (dust/water) that plague conventional sensor-based hub motors. |

themes.title: Auto components & EV-driveline localization
themes.need: Premiumization, content-per-vehicle rise and EV/hybrid transition pull a deep auto-ancillary chain - MOTHERSON/SONACOMS/BOSCHLTD/SCHAEFFLER/SKFINDIA/UNOMINDA-tier on driveline, bearings, wiring (MSUMI) and EV systems; OLAELEC/ATHERENERG/OLECTRA on EV OEMs (OLAELEC targeting cell-to-pack 10-15% cost edge); SUNDRMFAST/ENDURANCE/CRAFTSMAN/BHARATFORG on forgings/machining. Q1FY27 showed contracted pricing finally landing for Tier-2s: SSWL earned EBITDA/wheel of Rs 314 against Rs 262 YoY, which management attributed mostly to two years of OEM input-price increases finally landing (1-5%, more pending) rather than mix, with all plants above 95% utilisation and knuckles at 100%; KROSS delivered a 12.23% EBITDA margin (+63bps) BEFORE two retrospective pass-throughs land (steel settled ~15 July, the CV conversion-cost settlement still pending), making Q1 a floor rather than a peak.
themes.driver: GST 2.0 demand pull; retrospective OEM price pass-throughs still to land (KROSS CV conversion cost); EV cell/Gigafactory ramps (OLAELEC 6GWh by June); export + new-platform content wins.

themes.title: Electronics manufacturing (EMS) & Make-in-India localization
themes.need: PLI + import-substitution + global China+1 sourcing drive an electronics-manufacturing build-out across consumer durables, defence and components. AMBER/PGEL/EPACK/SYRMA/AVALON/CYIENTDLM on box-build/EMS; DIXON-tier scale; CPPLUS/CNL on surveillance; KAYNES/SYRMA on integrated components; appliance ODMs (EPACK, AMBER) ride RAC/white-goods localization.
themes.driver: PLI disbursement + new ODM/OEM program wins; appliance season; defence/aero EMS conversion (AVALON, CYIENTDLM).

hero.oneLiner: A technology-led Tier-1 supplier of critical, control-intensive Electronic Control Units (ECUs) — including India-pioneered Integrated Starter Generator (ISG) and Sensorless ISG technology — to 2&3-wheeler, generator and electric-vehicle OEMs in India, the US and Europe.

one_liner.title: One Liner (RHP)
one_liner.body: A technology-led Tier-1 supplier of critical, control-intensive Electronic Control Units (ECUs) — including India-pioneered Integrated Starter Generator (ISG) and Sensorless ISG technology — to 2&3-wheeler, generator and electric-vehicle OEMs in India, the US and Europe.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: SEDEMAC designs, develops and manufactures in-house control-intensive ECUs - including sensorless integrated starter generator (ISG), electronic fuel injection (EFI), combined ISG+EFI ECUs and EV motor control units for two/three-wheelers, and genset controllers and genset EFI ECUs for the industrial market. Critical, control-intensive products contributed 86.53% of revenue for the nine months ended December 31, 2025. The company originated from an IIT Bombay lab in 2007 and sells directly to OEMs, integrating proprietary technology into their platforms.

group_structure.title: Group structure (subsidiaries / JV / related parties)
group_structure.body: - None — group company: The company states it has no group company as on the date of the RHP

products.title: Products & brands
products.body:
- **Mobility (2/3W):** ISG ECUs, EFI ECUs, ISG+EFI ECUs, EV Motor Control Units (MCUs)
- **Industrial (Genset):** Genset Controllers (GC) with integrated electronic governing (eGov), Genset EFI ECUs, Automatic Mains Failure (AMF) genset controllers

end_markets.title: End Markets (RHP)
end_markets.body:
- Indian 2&3-wheeler (ICE and electric) market
- Indian and global power generator market
- US and European OEM customers
- Emerging Commercial Vehicle market (under development)
- Power Tools market (under development)

cost_leadership.title: Supply chain integration (RHP report)
cost_leadership.body: Indian Tier-I supplier selling directly to OEMs; proprietary control technologies conceived and developed entirely in-house with full control across design, engineering and manufacturing at two Pune facilities (MF1, MF2). Imported raw materials (principally electronic components/semiconductors from global distributors such as Avnet, Arrow, Edom, Rabyte, WPG) were 43%-54% of revenue across the periods; supplier arrangements are on purchase orders, not long-term contracts. Company earns export incentives and grants (Duty Drawback, RoDTEP, Maharashtra Electronics Policy 2016, M-SIPS) totalling 0.35%-1.18% of revenue.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Sustained revenue growth (24.75% CAGR FY23-FY25) driving operating leverage
- Profit-for-year margin expansion from 2.03% (FY23) to 7.15% (FY25) to 9.28% (9M FY26) via operating leverage, improved product mix and operational efficiency
- Margin/cash-flow benefits from in-house proprietary technology and full control across design, engineering and manufacturing

capital_allocation.title: Strategy & capital allocation
capital_allocation.body:
- Continue initiating and scaling breakthrough control technologies across mobility and industrial markets
- Deepen penetration of EV motor control units (MCU shipments grew from 9,364 in FY24 to 45,731 in 9M FY26)
- Expand genset EFI ECU adoption globally (genset EFI units grew from 13,768 in FY23 to 221,616 in 9M FY26)
- Leverage cross-market technology use, procurement synergies and OEM partnerships

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: Registered office relocated to Baner, Pune (September 26, 2025). The DRHP is an Offer for Sale only; no fresh-issue-funded capacity expansion project is described in the routed COMPANY sections.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- First-to-market advantage: first in India to develop sensorless commutation (SLC) based ISG ECUs for 2/3W ICE vehicles; pioneered integrated electronic governing in genset controllers (2014)
- Market leadership: ~35% domestic ISG ECU market share (2W+3W, volume, 9M FY26, among top 4); ~75%-77% India genset controller share and ~14% global share (FY25)
- In-house proprietary control technologies developed end-to-end; critical control-intensive products were 86.53% of revenue (9M FY26)
- Deep technical nucleus: >600 man-years of engineering contribution from IIT/NIT/BITS engineers; >200 man-years in the core nucleus
- Integrated design, engineering and manufacturing enabling rapid innovation and cost efficiency
- Cumulatively sold more than 10 million control-intensive products to automotive and genset markets as of December 31, 2025

risks.title: Bear — key risks
risks.body:
- Extreme customer concentration in TVS Motor — TVS Motor contributed 75.48%-83.46% of revenue across the periods; top-3 customers 87.76%-91.22%; loss or reduced demand would materially hurt revenue and cash flows
- Single-segment/product dependence — Mobility segment (2/3W ISG/EFI) is ~85% of revenue; ISG/EFI/ISG+EFI ECUs are ~98%-99% of mobility control-intensive volume
- Technology transition and OEM acceptance risk — Revenue depends on OEMs adopting new proprietary technologies through multi-year validation; non-regulatory changes carry acceptance risk
- Export/geographic exposure — Significant genset unit exports to US and Europe expose the company to trade policy, tariffs and FX
- Reliance on commissioned CRISIL industry report — Industry and market-share data derive from a report exclusively commissioned and paid for by the company
- Promoter holding relatively low — Promoters hold only 22.26% on a fully diluted basis pre-Offer

commitments.title: Promises (RHP)
commitments.body:
- **Scale EV motor control unit (MCU) shipments in the two/three-wheeler market**
- **Grow genset EFI ECU adoption and exports across US, Europe and India**
- **Continue initiating and scaling new-to-market control technologies as first player in India**
- **Sustain leadership in ISG ECU (2W/3W) and genset controllers**

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Grow into a global leader in ECUs for small powertrains by leveraging synergy across seemingly unrelated markets — 2&3-wheelers (ICE and electric), Power Tools, small Commercial Vehicles, small Tractors, Small Generators and Outdoor Powered Equipment.
- Commonize motor-controller components and designs across these small-powertrain markets (similar power/voltage ratings) to accumulate volumes and gain sourcing/supply-chain scale benefits.
- Extend the ISG+EFI combined ECU proposition to accelerate the ICE-powered 2&3-wheeler market's shift towards adopting ISG as a default.
